@graph.name: docs
@graph.summary: Documentation ABOUT the knowledge graph — how the harness works, what its directories hold, how a process runs. Rendered by the plain just-the-docs pipeline. Distinct from `folio`, which is content an author CREATES using the graph; the difference is the SUBJECT, not the format. An L1 library's catalogue is `library/`; a note about it is a `folio`; the page explaining how ingestion works is `docs`.

@graph.name: library
@graph.summary: L1 source content — one `<bib-slug>/` per ingested document, holding `sections/*.md`, `structure.json` and, where the source was scanned, `ocr/page-NNN.txt`. Every knowledge-graph reference to a source resolves through here, never to a loose path or a bare URL.

@graph.name: web-app
@graph.summary: A web app held as source and published as its own chrome-less page, built at publish by the web-app-build Tool and loaded only when a reader opens its route.

@graph.name: document-kinds
@graph.summary: Document kinds — named structures of sections (fixed or semi-fixed) that a document authored with a harness follows, one `document-kind/1.0.0` JSON each, plus computed `document-kind-coverage/1.0.0` reports of how a subject realises one. Every kind and section names its sources; `computedFrom` names the declared graphs a section derives from.

@graph.name: translation-sources
@graph.summary: POT templates, PO catalogues and their `TranslationNode` manifests, one directory per target locale. The INPUT to injection; the rendered output is ordinary content that declares its own `lang`.

@graph.name: openapi
@graph.summary: OpenAPI 3 documents a layer holds, each verbatim beside a provenance node naming the repository, path and commit it was ingested from (cat-harness's `openapi` subgraph). Every operation in a document is a node of its own: a page and an IRI under the layer's docs.

@graph.name: archimate
@graph.summary: ArchiMate models a layer holds, as Archi `.archimate` files (plain XML or Archi's zipped archive), named by `cat-archimate.config.json` (cat-harness's `archimate` subgraph). Every view, element and relationship in a model is a node of its own: a page and an IRI, keyed by Archi's own id, and every view is drawn as SVG from the model's diagram.

@graph.name: fhir-artifact-index
@graph.summary: The artefact index of a published FHIR Implementation Guide, reconstructed from its published output — every artefact by canonical URL and published representation, with the IG API's JSON Schema / JSON-LD sidecars as an overlay where the IG publishes them. No IG publishes such an index itself, so every field records which file it came out of.

@graph.name: ig-ast
@graph.summary: The IG Publisher's abstract syntax tree of a FHIR Implementation Guide (its resources, their dependency edges and the build plan), ingested into the folio that uses the IG. One branch per IG package id; the IG's own source need not be materialised.

@graph.name: ig-pages
@graph.summary: The pages of a FHIR Implementation Guide mirror, generated from its artefact index and the chrome of its template chain. Carried beside `docs` on the same directory: `docs` is how the site mounts them, and this kind is what says they are derived.

@graph.name: catalogue
@graph.summary: A remote catalogue modelled by reference — communities, collections and items of a corpus the layer does not hold. Every node declares whether its bytes are here (`materialized`), elsewhere (`referenced`) or unestablished (`unknown`), with no default. Distinct from `library`, which is content that IS here.

@graph.name: glossary
@graph.summary: SKOS terms (folio-glossary/v1): local terms with definitions and codes, linked to external SKOS schemes by exactMatch rather than copied. Rendered on the glossary/ page.

@graph.name: smart-trust-ast
@graph.description: WHO SMART Trust's IG Publisher AST, ingested although the IG's source is not. Read from the branch family `cat/fhir-harness/fhir-ast/` on `litlfred/smart-trust`, one branch per IG package id; this IG's is `cat/fhir-harness/fhir-ast/smart.who.int.trust`. Restored by `fhir-harness/scripts/ig-cache.sh`; never in the checkout.

@graph.name: smart-trust-artifact-index
@graph.description: The IG's artefact index. `index.json`, `menu.json`, `releases.json`, `package.tgz` and `sidecars/` are not committed: fhir-harness's `ig-index:build` writes them at publish from the IG's AST (`sidecars/` through smart-base's `ig-site:sidecars` step). Only `README.md` is committed. `index.json` carries a `provenance` block naming the AST or config file each field came from.

@graph.name: smart-trust-document-kinds
@graph.description: How this IG realises the document kinds of the layers it needs: `dak.coverage.smart-trust.json`, the DAK view of `fhir-artifact-index/`, which places each artefact in one of the ten DAK components by its FHIR resource type and lists what no rule places. Generated at publish, after the index it reads, by the DAK layer's `gen-document-kinds.ts` (`bun run cat smart-base:document-kinds`); not committed.

@graph.name: smart-trust-openapi
@graph.description: The OpenAPI documents this instance holds, ingested by the cat-openapi harness from the sources `cat-openapi.config.json` names: the trust network gateway's API, which the published IG carries as a vendored Swagger UI and which `ingest-ig-artifacts.ts` does not treat as the IG's own API. Each document is held verbatim beside a `<id>.source.json` recording the repository, path and commit it was read from. Each operation is a node with a page and an IRI (`gateway/<operationId>/`, `gateway/<operationId>.jsonld`), written by `cat-openapi/scripts/gen-openapi-pages.ts`; the pages are complete HTML that fetch the document beside them, so `served` publishes them as they are.

@graph.name: smart-trust-docs
@graph.description: The artefact pages of smart-trust's IG site, generated from `fhir-artifact-index/index.json` by `smart-trust:pages` (`fhir-harness/scripts/gen-ig-pages.ts`) with smart-base's themes, built at publish and never committed. They build into the IG's own site at `/smart-trust/`, under the IG's menu; the IG's own index, toc and artifacts pages are the site's landing pages. `instanceRoot: true` makes this directory answer at `/smart-trust/`. It is declared here, not in `cat-harness.json`, because `compose-docs` treats every docs entry there as a composition layer and would overlay this instance's `index.md` onto the main site's.

@graph.name: library
@graph.description: L1 source documents materialized for smart-trust: the GDHCN Administrative and Operational Framework 1.2 (9 October 2026), the legal source for GDHCN definitions and Trust Domains. Every knowledge-graph reference to the Framework resolves through here, and `check:materialized-fixity` verifies its SHA-256 digest against `catalogue/`.

@graph.name: smart-trust-catalogue
@graph.description: Qualified Dublin Core (`folio-dublin-core/v1`) and catalogue node (`folio-catalogue-node/v1`) records for two kinds of item: the document materialized in `library/` (the GDHCN Administrative and Operational Framework 1.2), and every work the IG cites that is not ingested, as a `referenced` item whose record is the IG's bibliography entry for it, keyed by the citation (`#ref-<slug>`). A capture of a cited work, when one exists, is kept in the repository's `uploads/` data store, which is not part of the KG. `bun run cat check:catalogue` and `bun run cat check:materialized-fixity` verify every node, metadataRef, libraryId, localPath and SHA-256 digest.

@graph.name: glossary
@graph.description: The primary GDHCN glossary (`gdhcn.glossary.json`, folio-glossary/v1): the 21 definitions in Section II of the GDHCN Administrative and Operational Framework 1.2, quoted from the L1 copy in `library/`. The Framework is the legal source; IG-only terms go in a separate scheme and never override it. Rendered and checked by `check:glossary`.

@graph.name: smart-trust-translations
@graph.description: The gettext side of smart-trust's own strings, one directory per target locale: the `glossary/` templates of the GDHCN glossary (`glossary/gdhcn.glossary.json`). A scheme's translations sit with the instance whose terms they translate. Written by `bun run cat glossary:pot`.

@graph.name: onboarding-game
@graph.description: The GDHCN onboarding game, "Join the Network" (Vite, TypeScript, three.js; Apache-2.0, from carlsbox/gdhcn-onboarding-game, see NOTICE). Declared by web-app.json and built and published by the harness's `apps` visualiser (Tool web-app-build) at <locale>/<harness>/apps/onboarding-game/, with no site chrome; nothing else on the site loads it. Its UI strings are translated through translations/<locale>/apps/ (smart-trust#176, Q-GAME-5).

@graph.name: archimate
@graph.description: The GDHCN trust network as ArchiMate (cat-harness's archimate subgraph): this guide's actors (input/fsh/actors/actors.fsh), the public keys and the trust list, and the three steps onboard, distribute and verify, as the home page's figure (input/images/trust_network.png) in a view with every box where the figure draws it. Built by archimate/build.py (`check:archimate` fails when the committed model is stale); the archimate-pages visualiser draws the view as SVG, and archimate/pretty.py draws it again in the original figure's style (input/includes/trust-network-pretty.svg).
